    How it works?

    Setup. Save your Tarkov Market API key in Settings and select a character. Prices follow that character's PVP, PVE or SEASON mode.

    Find an item. Use English item names and open Inspect in the game. Automatic scanning checks it after a left-click. Or click Scan now and return to the game within 3 seconds, or enter an English name and click Search.

    Prices. Flea Market shows the best and 24-hour average prices. Trader shows the best trader price. Values in parentheses are prices per slot.

    Stock. Stock shows available quantity / collection target. Tarkov Market supplies the total quantity. Found in Raid and Regular stock are kept separately in a local save. Regular and Found in Raid show fixed requirements; Shared and Shared (FiR) include other eligible items.

    Stock controls. F1 adds one Found in Raid item, F2 adds one Regular item, F3 removes one Found in Raid item, and F4 removes one Regular item. Unavailable actions are disabled, including additions to covered requirements and removals from empty stock. Change or disable these shortcuts in Settings.

    Goals. Next Item lists the item's quests and hideout upgrades. Their ratios use your locally recorded Found in Raid and Regular stock. Brown checkmarks mark completed goals.

    Completed Item. When all listed goals are completed and no active item requirement remains, only the completed goal list is shown. Stock, requirement rows and stock buttons are hidden.

    Names and refresh. The brown copy icons copy only the item, quest or hideout name. Refresh progress reloads Market data. The last goal details stay visible during refreshes.

    Saving. Stock updates immediately and saves the total to Market in the background. The Found in Raid / Regular split is saved locally for the selected character and game mode. Wait for pending saves before exiting. Unsaved stock changes are not replayed after restart; confirmed item quality is saved locally. Closing either window closes both. Text recognition runs locally.
